newsitem.title: USA: New England Electric plans divestments.
newsitem.headline: New England Electric plans divestments.

text.p: New England Electric System said Monday it agreed to put its power generating businesses on sale as part of statewide plan to foster competition in the Massachusetts electricity industry.

New England said it was announcing the divestment plan in anticipation of a proposed settlement under which its Massachusetts Electric Co and New England Power Co subsidiaries agreed to implement Massachusetts Attorney General Scott Harshbarger's "Consumers First" restructuring plan.
The settlement agreement is expected to be filed Tuesday with the Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities.
The Consumers First plan would open utility wires to competitive electricity suppliers in 1998. It is expected to result in savings of at least 10 percent for customers.
New England Electric System said that in return for its commitment to divest its fossil and hydroelectric generating businesses, it was assured recovering investments made under the old rules.
As part of the plan, the system will also divest its regulated oil and gas business, and potentially its minority interests in five operating nuclear plants in four New England states, it said.
